speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe exactly how your leg is positioned right now, and did you hear a "pop" or snap when the accident happened? Also, are you able to move your big toe independently?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the specific nature of that right groin pain—does it feel like a deep ache, sharp stabbing, or is there a sensation of instability? Additionally, when you tried to lift your right leg today, did you notice any clicking or grinding sounds, and are you currently able to walk on that leg at all?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Hip Dislocation (Posterior).

Based on the classic presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated right leg following a rear-end collision, this is highly indicative of a posterior hip dislocation. Immediate reduction is required to prevent permanent neurological damage. I am requesting the Orthopedic_Specialist for immediate bedside reduction and an Emergency_Room_XRay to confirm joint alignment and rule out associated fractures.
